hypothesis: The e<=0.9 ceiling on linear accel_step decodability (layer-4 R2 about 0.37-0.41 on data_seed 1 at 3000 steps) is a real ceiling and not slow convergence. Setup is identical to exp-20261016-054409-8a30 (N=64, 4 layers, d_model=64, m2 in [0.1, 1], e in [0, 0.9], data_seed 1, best-of-5 controls) except training runs 6000 steps. Seed 70 is included because it was the one seed still rising after step 1000. The final layer-4 accel_step R2 from probes_final, unrounded, rises by no more than 0.03 over the same seed's 3000-step endpoint (seed 70: 0.36862, run-20261016-081926-7b68; seed 71: 0.41131, run-20261016-081926-e120). Endpoints are compared because the lr schedule depends on run length. Within-run growth between steps 3000 and 6000, read as layer-4 control plus margin, is reported for description only. Both reference run IDs are cited.
expected_if_true: Final layer-4 accel_step R2 is <= 0.399 (seed 70) and <= 0.441 (seed 71). Both are still below 0.50 and still beat their controls.
expected_if_false: Final layer-4 accel_step R2 is >= 0.429 (seed 70) or >= 0.471 (seed 71) in at least one seed, which would mean the e<=0.9 ceiling partly reflects undertraining. Values that fall between these bands are inconclusive.
